findings.section: Task 2: `Progress` — the determinate bar, on Base UI
findings.title: Base UI `Progress` does not clamp, so two of Task 2's four tests can never pass
findings.verdict_note: All quotes verbatim (436, 465, 466, 474, 515, 524). I verified the API claim against the INSTALLED package rather than the reviewers' word: `@base-ui/react` 1.6.0 at node_modules/.pnpm/@base-ui+react@1.6.0_.../progress/root/ProgressRoot.mjs:52 sets `'aria-valuenow': value ?? undefined` with no clamp, and `utils/valueToPercent.mjs` is a bare `(value - min) * 100 / (max - min)`. A grep for `Math.min`, `Math.max` and `clamp` across the entire `progress/` directory returns nothing. So `value={1.8}` renders `aria-valuenow="180"` and `value={-0.5}` renders `"-50"` — both asserted tests fail. This is a wrong-ARIA bug as well as a test failure, because the plan itself states the over-unity case is genuinely reachable (a compressed response reports encoded `total` against decoded `loaded`).
findings.whats_wrong: Task 2 Step 4 says 'Expected: PASS — 4 tests', but two can never go green on the installed package, and the implementer is left deciding whether to fix the component or loosen the test while three places in the document insist Base UI clamps. Because the over-unity case is real, a shipped bar would also announce 'one hundred eighty percent' to a screen reader and paint an indicator 180 % wide.
findings.proposed_fix: Clamp in `Progress.tsx` with `Math.min(100, Math.max(0, value * 100))` and correct the three places that claim Base UI clamps — this component comment, the Step 3 blockquote's 'deletes a manual clamp' line (436) and the over-unity test's comment (465).
findings.why_it_works: The clamp lives in the one wrapper that owns the fraction-to-percent conversion, so both asserted tests pass and the real compressed-response case can no longer produce an out-of-range `aria-valuenow`; the indeterminate branch is untouched, which is the part Base UI genuinely does own.

Central claim verified in the installed playwright-core 1.61.1: `computeBox(element)` (lib/coreBundle.js) returns `visible: rect.width > 0 && rect.height > 0` after an `isElementStyleVisibilityVisible` check — there is no opacity term anywhere in the computation, so an `opacity: 0` element with a box is VISIBLE to Playwright. The span is always mounted (line 1253-1264) and only animates opacity (line 1257). The reviewer's counterpart assertion is buildable — `toHaveCSS` is standard Playwright. Related to but not line-conflicting with L2-17, which adds a manual check in Task 5 Step 6; L2-20 covers only the focus path (the stepper keeps focus), L2-17 also covers hover, so both are worth applying.
findings.whats_wrong: The only automated check over the percentage-visibility rule cannot fail. Playwright treats a zero-opacity element with a non-empty box as visible, so this assertion passes whether or not the reveal variants ever fire — meaning the exact Tailwind behaviour the plan flags as its one unverified risk is the risk this assertion is blind to.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `toBeVisible()` on the percentage with `toHaveCSS('opacity', '1')`, and add a counterpart asserting `'0'` while the control is still at written speed.
findings.why_it_works: Computed opacity is the property the visibility rule actually drives, so the assertion fails exactly when the reveal breaks — which `toBeVisible` structurally cannot do.
